findings.reason: consolidating three writers and one deleter into a single owner needs a census command that actually enumerates them, else a site is left behind and the "every create and delete lives in one module" claim is false.
findings.text: §8 rests its writer census on `grep 'MERGE (sg)-\[r?e?l?:MAPS_TO_IMAS\]' imas_codex/` and states it "finds exactly these three", but that BRE pattern treats `?` literally, so the command returns 0 matches; the three real writers are imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2008, imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:367 and imas_codex/ids/models.py:580 (written `[r:MAPS_TO_IMAS]` and `[rel:MAPS_TO_IMAS]`), and the "only delete site" claim for _clear_mapping (imas_codex/cli/map.py:661) carries no census command at all

findings.reason: the retirement is a partial census; the claim filter and the reset would keep reading and nulling a property the plan deletes, so §8 must name every site before removing the fields.
findings.text: §8 states SignalSource "loses mapping_target_path and mapping_target_ids" and names only workers.py:237 as the reader, but those scalars are read or written at four sites in that file: the claim predicate `AND sg.mapping_target_ids = $ids_name` (workers.py:213), the projection target_ids/target_path/target_type (workers.py:236–238), the reset filter `AND sg.mapping_target_ids IN $ids_names` (workers.py:380) and the null-out of all three fields (workers.py:392–394)

findings.reason: either route enrichment's claim through the new owner or state why the parameterised routine cannot serve it; otherwise the same duplicate recurs for the deferred families (base/grouping.py and mdsplus/graph_ops.py) the plan names.
findings.text: §7 adds a generic claim routine to imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py and defers grouping.py's family as "a different lifecycle stage", but grouping.py's claim_signal_sources (grouping.py:92) claims the same `SignalSource` label with the same ORDER BY rand() + claim_token two-step pattern, and §7's own parameterisation (label, status predicate, claim property names, returned fields) already covers it — so the plan knowingly leaves two claim implementations on one label inside one package

findings.reason: the section must name, in its own text, what it retires or merges in the CLI-option family, or state why nothing can be, as the rubric requires.
findings.text: §7 adds the `discover map` subcommand with five options, the `DISCOVERY_DOMAINS` value "map" (imas_codex/cli/discover/common.py:30) and status/clear dispatch branches, but names no cli_option it retires or merges for that addition: the "seven helpers become three" merge is a public_definitions change and the two retired options belong to §8, not §7

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the candidate stage hides retrieval, judgment and routing behind candidates.py's retrieve_candidates/judge_candidates/route, and §7 places the generalised claim routines in the shared owner imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py rather than in a new module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §8's retirement of the mapping_target_* scalars names one reader where imas_codex/ids/workers.py holds four read/write sites, and §7 leaves a second same-label claim implementation beside the owner it creates.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §7 adds five CLI options and a subcommand (cli_options family) without naming any cli_option it retires or merges.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's account of the existing MAPS_TO_IMAS writers is asserted through a grep that returns zero matches, so its prior-art search for the edge machinery is not shown to see the sites it consolidates.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §10 deletes the _capture_decisions_cost monkeypatch and extends the existing PipelineCost/_acall_llm cost path (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:78) rather than layering a wrapper over it; §7 reuses run_discovery_engine and OrphanRecoverySpec rather than adding a second engine.
